content.text: Dan Mordaunt exposes bookkeeper Talbot’s plan to rob Barton & Rogers, helps police arrest the burglars, and earns $1,000. Talbot is imprisoned. Dan later rescues abducted Althea from Donovan’s liquor saloon in Brooklyn by trapping Donovan in the cellar. Harriet Vernon then moves into a Madison Avenue house with Dan, his mother, and Althea, adopting Dan. Years later, repentant Robert Davis restores money stolen from Dan’s father, enabling Dan to become a business partner. The text then shifts to Samuel Pepys’s diary, describing London offices, homes, courts, theatres, taverns, illnesses, family disputes, and court life. Finally, a socialist narrative portrays impoverished Mugsborough workers exploited by Rushton’s firm through low wages, unsafe conditions, rushed and dishonest work, surveillance, unemployment, and class contempt.
